subject: Meridian: reserved tenor, GPU-shock mitigation & discount approval path
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Meridian: reserved tenor, GPU-shock mitigation & discount approval path

Alex — following our call yesterday, attaching two artifacts (commit options workbook + draft SOW) with the three commercial paths we discussed. High level asks:

- Can you confirm whether Meridian is open to a 24-month committed pool with phased activation (Q1/Q3 ramp), OR a 12-month commit with a quarterly price-collar adjustment?
- Meridian asked for a discount floor in the event GPU market prices spike — we can propose a shock-buffer credit pool instead of straight indexation.

Attached: Meridian_commit_options_v3.xlsx (breakouts by SKU/tenor) and SOW_draft_Meridian_v1.pdf.

Quick context for the internal team (cc'd): Meridian is sensitive to long lock-ins but needs predictable capacity for their imaging workloads starting Sep 2026. They want protection against GPU price inflation and clarity on discount escalation approvals if we offer more aggressive terms.

Next steps I'm proposing: internal posture + one-pager of approved concession limits before I respond to procurement. Need a recommended pricing floor and the approval authority (who signs off on >20% discount or credits).

Thanks — Sergio

-- 
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: Meridian_commit_options_v3.xlsx (xlsx), SOW_draft_Meridian_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@meridianhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 10:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meridian: reserved tenor, GPU-shock mitigation & discount approval path

Sergio — thanks for the deck and the call notes. Meridian's procurement lean is toward shorter contractual risk and operational predictability. A few items: 

1) We're inclined to a 12-month committed pool with quarterly re-evaluation tied to an external GPU price index (we can share a vendor index). We want downside protection if prices drop, and a cap if prices spike.
2) The ‘shock-buffer credit pool’ you mentioned sounds promising — would prefer credits instead of retroactive price increases to preserve budgeting simplicity for our internal teams.
3) On discounts: Meridian procurement can approve up to 15% off list with internal signoffs; anything beyond that needs a commercial exec approval and legal review.

Can you send your recommended contract language (short clause) for the credit pool and the proposed approval ladder for discounts >15%? Procurement is tight on legal redlines so clarity helps.

Best,
Alex Reed
Senior Director, IT Infrastructure
Meridian Health
alex.reed@meridianhealth.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Meridian: reserved tenor, GPU-shock mitigation & discount approval path

Sergio / team — reviewed Alex's note and the workbook. Quick modeling points and asks: 

- Assumptions used: baseline GPU basket price = $3.20/hour (current mix), projected volatility +/- 30% over 12 months.
- Financial impact: 12-month commit with 10% discount vs 24-month commit with 18% discount — the latter gives ~12% lower expected cost over 24 months but increases exposure to upside shocks in months 13–24.

Proposals to balance risk: 
- Option A (customer-preferred): 12-month commit + quarterly price-collar band (if index > +25% over baseline, Redwood sends credits equal to the excess tokens up to a buffer pool; if index < -15%, Meridian gets the benefit via retroactive credit to the following quarter).
- Option B (our favorable): 24-month phased commit (year 1 smaller reserve) with a one-time reprice window at month 12 if index deviates >30%. The trade-off: better unit economics vs. longer lock.

Approval ladder required for discounts/credits: 
- <=15% discount or credits pool size <= $150k: Sales Ops (Hannah) + Finance (Neha) signoff.
- 15% < discount <= 25% or credits pool <= $500k: Head of Commercial (Marissa) + Finance approval.
- >25% or credits pool > $500k: VP Commercial + CFO signoff (exec review).

Questions for Sales: What is the minimum acceptable NRR and margin floor for Meridian? I included sensitivity tabs in the attached workbook (Meridian_commit_options_v3.xlsx) — please review and call out the target band so I can finalize recommended thresholds.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Finance — Commercial Deals | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 14:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Meridian: reserved tenor, GPU-shock mitigation & discount approval path

Thanks Neha — I like the approach. Two operational notes before we present back to Meridian procurement: 

1) Recommend we lead with Option A (12-month + quarterly collar + shock-buffer credits). Why: aligns with their procurement preference, limits long-dated exposure, and keeps us positioned to upsell in Q4 if usage proves out.

2) Shock-buffer mechanics (draft language):
- Redwood will maintain a non-refundable Shock Buffer Credit Pool for the term equal to X% of committed spend (TBD in workbook). Credits are applied quarterly against overage invoices when the agreed GPU index exceeds the baseline by more than the collar threshold. Credits do not reduce committed minimums but offset variable usage charges.

3) Discount/credit approval workflow (operational):
- If negotiated concession sits within Neha's <=15% band, Sales Ops will execute and record via HubSpot and internal approval doc.
- For concessions between 15–25%, Marissa (Head of Commercial) must sign; legal must vet the shock-buffer clause.
- For anything above 25% or any structural change to tenor/termination rights, escalate to VP Commercial + Finance (CFO).

Action for Sergio: please confirm you want me to present Option A + the shock-buffer clause to Alex and procurement. If yes, I'll schedule a short call with Meridian procurement and include legal (1 PRD + one redline-ready SOW).

If you want the 24-month variant on the table as a fallback, say so — but we should price it as a conditional counter-offer (better unit economics in exchange for extended lock and stronger termination penalties).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
